subject: Post-call: qualification + hyperscaler delta & 1M-token test plan
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Aiden Ross <aiden@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: qualification + hyperscaler delta & 1M-token test plan

Hi Aiden — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary goal: reduce inference spend for your customer-facing chat (multi-tenant SaaS) while keeping 95th percentile latency < 120ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Current baseline: Hyperscaler managed endpoint (g4-like footprint) with no KV cache; procurement is sensitive to per-1M token spend.
- Constraints: data residency US, strict audit log requirements, and procurement wants a simple TCO comparison to justify migration.

What Redwood can test & deliver (proposed):
1) 1M-token synthetic run comparing: Hyperscaler-managed model, Hyperscaler with our quantized variant, Redwood hosted baseline, Redwood with prefix/KV caching enabled.
   - Metrics: cost per 1M tokens, 50th/95th latency, tail p99, and effective tokens/sec.
2) Batching sensitivity sweep: batch sizes [1, 4, 8, 16] with two cold/warm cache conditions to estimate real-world per-request latencies and batching benefit.
3) Cache hit-rate scenarios: 0%, 30%, 60% to show delta in per-token cost and latency.
4) Operational notes: breakdown of required infra, SLA delta, and any integration blockers (we'll include sample audit log exports and KMS integration checklist).

Deliverables & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): sign-off on scope + sample prompt set (you to share ~100 representative prompts).
- Week 1: run 1M-token synthetic across 3 configurations and share the raw cost model + readout.
- Week 2: run batching + cache sensitivity tests and present a concise deck with recommendations.

Ask: can you share the sample prompt set and confirm the procurement contact for the formal TCO artefact? Also flag if we should include on-prem/private deployment runs in scope.

Attachments: I will attach a lightweight comparison matrix + the cost model we intend to use.

Thanks — I copied Ben and Karthik to loop them in on test design and billing assumptions.

—
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment stubs: redwood_vs_hyperscalers_matrix.pdf (summary), 1M_token_cost_model.xlsx (calculator)

Monica — this is excellent, thanks for the clear plan. Quick answers and clarifications: 

- We'll share the 100 prompts by EOD tomorrow. They are a mix of short support-style prompts (~40–80 tokens) and some longer generative prompts (~200–400 tokens).
- Procurement contact is "Procurement <procurement@acme-ai.com>" (looped). They'll want a per-1M token comparison and an appendix with assumed instance/VM costs.
- On-prem not needed for phase 1 — focus on hosted vs hyperscaler managed.

A couple of asks from our side:
1) Can you include an apples-to-apples per-token compute cost (GPU-hours normalized) so our infra folks can map to the current spend?
2) For the cache hit-rate scenarios, please show expected customer-visible latency (not just backend per-token).

Looking forward — will send prompts tomorrow.

Cheers,
Aiden
Aiden Ross

Aiden / team — adding a bit more colour on the test matrix and things we'll capture: 

Proposed test matrix (parallelizable):
- Config A: Hyperscaler managed endpoint (baseline) — run with no explicit batching on client side.
- Config B: Hyperscaler + batched client (batch sizes 4 & 8), measure latency tail and token throughput.
- Config C: Redwood hosted model (same model family, quantized where applicable) — run with Redwood runtime batching (1,4,8,16) and prefix/KV cache toggled.

For each run we will capture: billable tokens, compute GPU-hours, average token latency, 50/95/99 latencies for entire request, and cost per 1M effective tokens after batching.

Caveats to call out now:
- Hyperscaler managed endpoints sometimes meter at a different token definition (we'll include meter-adjustment rows).
- Cold-start vs warm-run matters — we'll do a warm-up phase of ~50k tokens before measuring.

Operationally: if Procurement wants a PDF TCO appendix, we can produce a two-page executive summary and a detailed appendix (Doc link will be provided).

Proposed immediate action: once Aiden uploads prompt set, we'll run an internal dry run on Redwood infra to validate the workload distribution and then run the three configs in parallel (targeting 72 hours to finish tests).

—
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachment references: redwood_vs_hyperscalers_matrix.pdf (will populate after runs).
